title: Thread Layouts in CuTe DSL
critical_patterns: Linear Layout: 1D sequential mapping of threads to data elements
2D Layout: Mapping threads to a 2D grid for matrix operations
Tiled Layout: Each thread processes a tile of elements
Vectorized Layout: Threads access vector elements for SIMD operations
code_snippets:
@cute.kernel
def layout_2d(matrix: cute.Tensor):
    tx = cute.arch.thread_idx()[0]
    ty = cute.arch.thread_idx()[1]
    bx = cute.arch.block_idx()[0]
    by = cute.arch.block_idx()[1]
    TILE_X, TILE_Y = 16, 16
    i = bx * TILE_X + tx
    j = by * TILE_Y + ty
    if i < cute.shape(matrix)[0] and j < cute.shape(matrix)[1]:
        matrix[i, j] = process(matrix[i, j])
constraints: Ensure threads access consecutive memory for coalescing
Align base address to cache line (128 bytes)
Use warp-size multiples for thread counts
Avoid shared memory bank conflicts by adding padding
compressed_summary: Thread layouts in CuTe DSL are essential for optimizing GPU kernel performance. They determine how threads map to data, affecting memory access patterns and computation distribution. Key concepts include thread-to-data mapping, coalesced memory access, and bank conflict avoidance. Proper thread layouts ensure warp-level organization and efficient thread tile partitioning. Critical patterns include Linear Layout for 1D sequential mapping, 2D Layout for matrix operations, Tiled Layout for processing multiple elements per thread, and Vectorized Layout for SIMD operations. Code snippets illustrate good practices like ensuring coalesced access and avoiding bank conflicts. Constraints emphasize the importance of accessing consecutive memory, aligning addresses to cache lines, using warp-size multiples, and adding padding to avoid conflicts. The right thread layout can significantly enhance performance, providing up to 100× speedup by optimizing memory access and reducing conflicts. Best practices include ensuring coalesced access, using 2D layouts for matrices, adding padding to avoid bank conflicts, and vectorizing operations when possible. Avoid strided access patterns, shared memory bank conflicts, and non-warp-size thread counts to maintain optimal performance.
